title: KUJO — Trust at the speed of AI.
description: 18-slide investor briefing with source evidence, recorded execution and editable planning assumptions.

slides.title:
Trust at the
speed of AI.
slides.copy: The programming language and accountability infrastructure for agent-driven development.

slides.title: Software production is outpacing verification.
slides.copy: Agents can report completion. Teams still need a reviewable chain from requested work to release decision.

features.title: The claim
features.copy: “Tests passed. Ready to merge.” An illustrative agent statement.

features.title: The evidence
features.copy: Command, exit code, changed revision, environment and retained failure output.

features.title: The gap
features.copy: Useful logs already exist. Connecting them across tools and review boundaries remains work.

slides.title: Greater autonomy requires stronger accountability.
slides.copy: The cost of an unverified action grows as agents gain authority.
slides.note: Conceptual progression; not a measured adoption curve

features.title: Suggest code
features.copy: Human selects the change → diff review

features.title: Complete a task
features.copy: Agent edits and runs commands → execution records

features.title: Operate a workflow
features.copy: Retries and external effects → boundaries, recovery and approval

slides.title: AI use is broad. Trust remains conditional.
slides.copy: Adoption of AI assistance is not evidence of autonomous production deployment.

slides.title: Build with clarity. Operate with control.
slides.copy: The language is the long-term foundation. Existing tools offer an earlier route into engineering workflows.

features.title: Clarity
features.copy: Kujo language / Spec / Eval: explicit intent and testable outcomes.

features.title: Context
features.copy: MCP / CaseFile / RunLedger: useful inputs, debugging evidence and run records.

features.title: Control
features.copy: Dispatch / Workcell / ShipCheck: orchestration, bounded execution and release checks.

slides.title: Accountability spans the whole task.
slides.copy: Each component owns a specific responsibility. A reviewable workflow composes their artifacts explicitly.
slides.note: Composition map; not automatic end-to-end enforcement

features.title: Instruction → Context
features.copy: Spec / PackWrite → MCP and repository context

features.title: Execution → Evaluation
features.copy: Dispatch / Workcell → Eval result artifacts

features.title: Evidence → Review → Release
features.copy: CaseFile / RunLedger → reviewer → ShipCheck gate

slides.title: The foundation is already being built.

features.title: Reviewable artifact

slides.title: A claim becomes inspectable evidence.
slides.copy: Recorded local coding fixture: correct a post-money ownership calculation. Inspect what failed, what changed and what passed.

features.title: Request

features.title: Execution

features.title: Decision
features.copy: Eval checks the correction. Accept this fixture; no production release.

slides.title: Adopt the ecosystem before the language.
slides.copy: Keep application code in its existing language. Introduce accountability at the workflow boundary.
slides.note: T02–T04, T08 · tools have their own runtime dependencies

features.title: Today: wrap the task
features.copy: Use CaseFile for command evidence and Eval for explicit repository checks.

features.title: Then: control execution
features.copy: Adopt Dispatch or Workcell after validating the target environment and runtime pins.

features.title: Over time: go deeper
features.copy: Choose Kujo for new agent tooling where native language integration adds value.

slides.title: Start with teams already delegating engineering work.
